title: Infrastructure I/O Hidden Inside Domain Entities and Aggregates
pattern: An entity or aggregate executes repository/database queries, persistence operations, or out-of-process service calls inside business behavior instead of receiving the required domain data from explicit orchestration.
why_bad: Infrastructure latency, failures, lazy-loading exceptions, and transaction boundaries are hidden inside apparently domain-local behavior, complicating isolated reasoning and tests and coupling the model to data-access lifecycle details. The entity cannot be tested hermetically in memory without mocking databases, and the transactional and performance costs of business operations are obscured.
detection: Trace entity/aggregate methods that accept, retain, or import repositories, query modules, or external service clients to actual I/O calls. Cover two subcases: (1) an aggregate looking up another aggregate or product while performing a domain operation; (2) an entity issuing queries or writes to enforce a business policy. Repository-typed parameters or imports are leads, not sufficient evidence on their own.
counterexample: Application services explicitly coordinating persistence and infrastructure adapter implementations intentionally executing or bridging queries are outside scope. Domain services intended to coordinate logic across aggregates are not automatically entity violations; a genuinely pure domain service does not itself perform external I/O.
source: *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* by Vaughn Vernon (Chapter 10, p. 362-363; "Disconnected Domain Model"); Vaughn Vernon, *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* (2013), Chapter 2, "Collaboration Context", p. 515.
